reviewed_hash_basis: sha256 over the concatenation of .claude/scripts/epic-gate.sh, .claude/scripts/tests/plan-batches.test.sh, docs/HOOKS.md in that order; independently reproduced by the orchestrator before recording (byte-identical)
stop_condition: each round-3 fix re-verified as new code; every extraction on the plan path audited for rc-AND-shape discipline; the four-part pairing standard applied to every META leg, with leg 4 (runs the SHIPPED artifact) checked explicitly

r3_fix_assessment.basis: Per-line .u/.f extraction now has rc+emptiness discipline and BREAKs (epic-gate.sh:1357-1367) - orchestrator-verified. The upstream flat_pairs flattening at :1347 still checks rc only, so a successful-but-empty result yields zero loop bodies and empty alias arrays.

_pb_canonical_key removed (0 definitions, 0 calls - orchestrator-verified); _pb_path_has_symlink at :735 checks leaf and ancestors with -L including dangling links. Under-degrades filenames ending in newline, which command substitution strips before the helper sees them.

_PB_DEGRADE_BINDINGS_JSON is populated at :1470 before the CHILD-BINDING-GATE degradation at :1489. The premature-call defect is closed. A distinct ordering defect on the computation-failure path remains as R4-F5.
epic-gate.sh:411-415 and docs/HOOKS.md:2582 both now refer to a growing named guard list rather than a fixed cardinality.

findings.description: The alias-pass flattening fails open on a successful-but-empty or partial jq result. flat_pairs is checked for nonzero rc only, with no shape or cardinality check; an empty result executes zero loop bodies, never sets line_extract_failed, and leaves alias_units/alias_files/alias_abs empty, so the alias check silently does not happen and aliased units may co-batch.
findings.evidence: Orchestrator-verified by reading :1344-1356: only flat_rc is tested. This is the FIFTH instance in this slice of a failed/absent computation reading as 'nothing to check' rather than 'could not check'.
findings.suggested_fix: Verify the flattened result is an array whose length equals the sum of all files[] lengths, and degrade with set_computation_failed on any empty, partial, or mismatched result.

findings.description: validate-design's captured exit status is never tested. A validator that prints a shape-valid ok:true object and exits nonzero is trusted, allowing batching after the authoritative validation command failed.
findings.evidence: Orchestrator-verified: :1162 captures rc correctly via `vout=$(...) || vout_rc=$?`, but the guard at :1167 tests only vshape_ok. The sibling design-status ladder 38 lines earlier at :1129 tests `[ "$status_rc" -ne 0 ] || [ "$status_shape_ok" != "true" ]`. Two ladders in one file disagree on whether rc counts.
findings.suggested_fix: Degrade when `[ "$vout_rc" -ne 0 ] || [ "$vshape_ok" != "true" ]`, matching the design-status ladder, and add a leg where validate-design prints valid ok:true JSON and exits nonzero.

findings.description: Declared filenames are captured through command substitution, which strips trailing newline bytes. A path whose name ends in a newline is checked under a different spelling, so both -L and -ef can miss it while the batching reducer retains the original byte-distinct JSON strings and can co-batch an alias with its target.
findings.evidence: Reviewer executed `orig=$'alias\n'; got=$(jq -nr --arg f "$orig" '$f')` and observed original_len=6 extracted_len=5 equal=no. No control-character rejection exists in the canonical gate at :1231-1255.
findings.suggested_fix: Reject newline/control characters in declared paths at the canonical-path gate (reject, never sanitise - the bjx class), or use a length-preserving protocol and validate the decoded value against the original JSON.

findings.description: _pb_degrade contains unguarded jq assignments under global set -e. A failure at ordered_ids_json construction, .order extraction, entry construction, or batches assembly exits before _pb_finish and its advertised envelope fallback, producing NO degraded JSON at all - the safety net itself fails without emitting a refusal.
findings.evidence: Unguarded assignments at :913, :964, :970, :973 with set -e at :44. This is the documented `var=$(cmd)` errexit-at-the-assignment trap already recorded in LESSONS.md.
findings.suggested_fix: Give every jq operation in _pb_degrade explicit `cmd || rc=$?` handling plus a jq-independent final refusal path.

findings.description: When the degraded-plan topological computation fails, the code falls back to lexical task-id order, which emits a dependent before its prerequisite even though the dependency edge is known. An ordering that could not be computed must not be emitted as a runnable schedule.
findings.evidence: ordered_ids_json is initialised from LC_ALL=C sort at :912-913 and left unchanged on topo failure at :956-965. The spec itself constructs T-A-DEPENDENT/T-Z-PREREQ at plan-batches.test.sh:1048-1056 precisely to show lexical order is wrong.
findings.suggested_fix: Fail closed with an ordering-specific reason and no runnable plan when known edges could not be honoured. Same direction as 'a set difference that did not compute must never read as an empty one'.

findings.description: No leg exercises the SHIPPED artifact. The harness copies $CANON/*.sh into a fixture and sets EG to that copy, so every assertion labelled SHIPPED runs a copy. Leg 4 of the four-part pairing standard - the discriminator - is absent, and the labels assert otherwise.
findings.evidence: Orchestrator-verified: `grep -c '\$CANON/epic-gate\.sh'` over the spec returns 0; :193 is `cp "$CANON/"*.sh "$SCRIPTS/"` and :222 is `EG="$SCRIPTS/epic-gate.sh"`.
findings.suggested_fix: Run at least one restore-control leg through $CANON/epic-gate.sh while keeping fixture-local supporting scripts and data, and correct the SHIPPED labels on legs that are not.

findings.description: Section 4 is labelled the prescribed intersection META-test but never mutates the intersection predicate. It replaces the batching command's `|| batch_rc=$?` handler and forces the whole jq reducer to fail, so the leg would behave identically if the intersection guard were deleted - it is non-discriminating for the property it names.
findings.evidence: Mutation at :521-540 replaces only the batch_rc assignment; the marker at :550-556 exits the entire jq call. The real intersection expression at epic-gate.sh:1636-1638 is never mutated. Marker uniqueness was separately checked and is not stranded.
findings.suggested_fix: Mutate the intersection expression itself to an always-empty/no-conflict result, then assert the mutant CO-BATCHES conflicting units while the control keeps them separate - failure in the guard's specific way.

findings.description: The broken-jq control uses a nonexistent epic, so _pb_degrade is reached with zero children and skips its jq-dependent branch entirely. It cannot detect the set -e exits of R4-F4 while presenting itself as broad present-but-malfunctioning-jq coverage.
findings.evidence: Fixture id EPIC-R9H-NONEXISTENT at :1286 and :1322; early epic unreadability calls _pb_degrade without children at epic-gate.sh:1071-1074, and _pb_degrade skips the jq-heavy branch when $# == 0 at :869.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a shape-valid fixture with real children reaching a later degradation reason, injecting failures independently into each _pb_degrade jq assignment.

non_discriminating.why: Mutates failure recovery and kills the whole jq reducer; never changes the intersection predicate it claims to guard.
They execute $EG, a fixture copy created at :193, not the repository artifact under $CANON.

non_discriminating.leg: 9h broken-jq control as coverage of degradation internals
non_discriminating.why: The nonexistent epic supplies zero children, so the unsafe jq operations inside _pb_degrade never execute.

non_discriminating.leg: Sections 4 and 7 when python3 is unavailable
non_discriminating.why: Both print SKIPPING and let the script pass without recording a failed or skipped assertion.

notes: Review was read-only and did not run any test suite (L2 was executing concurrently). Reviewer ran rg/sed/nl/shasum, bash -n, and short in-memory probes. Both scoped bash files pass bash -n. The three HIGH findings were each independently re-verified by the orchestrator against the source before this artifact was recorded; the reviewed_hash was independently recomputed and matched byte-for-byte.
